property.name: dbt_user
property.description: Account that owns the dbt configuration directory. Analysts run dbt as themselves; this only owns what Ambari writes.

property.name: dbt_conf_dir
property.description: Where the connection profile is written. Point DBT_PROFILES_DIR here, which dbt-env.sh does for you.

property.name: dbt_profile_name
property.description: Name of the profile written to profiles.yml. A project that names a different profile still runs: pass --profile, or set this to the name the project expects.

property.name: dbt_target
property.description: Target inside the profile that dbt uses by default.

property.name: dbt_adapter_type
property.description:
The kind of warehouse dbt connects to, which decides both the adapter it loads and the shape of the profile. The package carries an adapter for each of trino, spark, impala, postgres, oracle, snowflake, bigquery, redshift, databricks, duckdb, athena, sqlserver, teradata and clickhouse. The four in the list below are rendered by the default profile template; any other value is rendered from its generic branch, which you complete by editing the template in the DBT profiles template configuration.
Hive is reached with spark: HiveServer2 speaks the same thrift protocol.

property.name: dbt_host
property.description: Host of the coordinator, HiveServer2, Impala daemon or database server the transformations run in, if there is one. Leave it empty to install dbt before the engine exists, or for a warehouse you configure by hand: the tool and its configuration directory are installed either way, and the profile is left as a commented placeholder until a host is given.

property.name: dbt_port
property.description: Port that host listens on: 8443 for a TLS Trino, 10000 for HiveServer2 thrift, 21050 for Impala, 5432 for PostgreSQL.

property.name: dbt_database
property.description: The catalog in Trino, the database elsewhere. Not used by the Spark and Hive profile, which addresses a schema directly.

property.name: dbt_schema
property.description: Schema the models are built in. dbt creates it if it is missing and the connecting identity may do so.

property.name: dbt_threads
property.description: How many models dbt builds at once. Each thread is one connection to the warehouse.

property.name: dbt_auth_method
property.description: How dbt authenticates to the warehouse. On a secured cluster this is kerberos, and people run dbt as themselves after kinit: no keytab is written into the profile, so every transformation appears in the engine's audit log as the person who ran it rather than as one shared identity.

property.name: dbt_connection_user
property.description: The user dbt presents to the warehouse. With Kerberos the ticket decides the identity and this is only what the client reports.

property.name: dbt_password
property.description: Only for username and password authentication.

property.name: dbt_jwt_token
property.description: Only for JWT authentication against Trino.

property.name: dbt_kerberos_service_name
property.description: Service part of the warehouse's principal: trino, hive or impala.

property.name: dbt_spark_method
property.description: How the Spark adapter reaches the server, when the warehouse type is spark. thrift is HiveServer2 and Spark thrift server; http is a Spark cluster endpoint; odbc needs a driver installed on these hosts.

property.name: dbt_ssl_verify
property.description: Path to the CA bundle used to verify the warehouse's certificate. Empty uses the system trust store.

property.name: content
property.description: Sourced by users before running dbt, so the profile and the tools are on the path.
